programme.title: Imagine...
programme.desc: Romantic, fearless, fantastical: delve into the thrilling world of Philip Pullman, and explore the author's own dark materials. Philip has been named both one of Britain's greatest writers and the most dangerous writer in Britain. He is best known for the much-loved `His Dark Materials' trilogy, which follows a young heroine, Lyra, through a series of heart-stopping adventures into other worlds.

programme.title: A Choral Pilgrimage with The Sixteen
programme.desc: Luminous choral music on the theme of peace, performed by one of the world's finest choirs and recorded at Peterborough Cathedral. A hymn to tranquillity, the concert features music from across nine centuries.

programme.title: Jane Goodall: Beauty and the Beasts
programme.desc: A closer look at primatologist Jane Goodall, who became accepted by a group of wild African chimpanzees and whose work transformed our understanding of man's closest relatives.

programme.title: Fred Dibnah's Building of Britain
programme.desc: Fred Dibnah shows how steam-powered machinery helped build Herefordshire's Eastnor Castle, and takes a look at the work of Augustus Welby Pugin, the architect whose buildings - such as the Palace of Westminster - were inspired by mediaeval gothic architecture.

programme.title: The Channel Tunnel: Life on the Inside
programme.desc: After 25 years in business, Eurotunnel is at a junction, with many of its staff facing retirement and new recruits being drafted in. Meanwhile the passenger comings and goings never stop and the summer is the busiest time of all, with super cars arriving in convoy for the Le Mans 24 hour race.

programme.title: Stolen: Catching the Art Thieves
programme.desc: In the early hours of 9 July 1994, the deputy director of London's Tate Gallery, Sandy Nairne, is woken with devastating news. Two of the gallery's most valuable paintings have been stolen while on loan to the Schirn gallery in Frankfurt, Germany.

programme.title: Call My Bluff
programme.desc: Robert Robinson presides over a duel of words and wit between Patrick Campbell, Felicity Kendal, Simon Ward, Frank Muir, Penelope Keith, and Joss Ackland.

programme.title: Face the Music
programme.desc: Question master Joseph Cooper invites viewers to match their musical wits against Patricia Owen, John Julius Norwich and David Attenborough. With guest musician Imogen Cooper.

programme.title: Bette Davis: The Benevolent Volcano
programme.desc: A look at the life of Hollywood star Bette Davis, spanning her life and career from the 1920s to the 1980s, on stage and on screen.

programme.title: Arena
programme.desc: Singer and writer George Melly takes a walk from his home in north London to the Hayward Gallery, reminiscing along the way about the influence of surrealism on his early life.

programme.title: The Great Philosophers
programme.desc: Bryan Magee and Bernard Williams discuss the work of French philosopher René Descartes.

programme.title: Patricia Routledge Remembers
programme.desc: Dame Patricia Routledge recalls how the character of Hyacinth Bucket first entered her life. She looks back on the part she played in bringing to life one of TV's most formidable comedy characters.

programme.title: Keeping Up Appearances
programme.desc: Richard forgets his wedding anniversary but then tells Hyacinth that he had a new alarm installed as an anniversary present, only he has forgotten the code.

programme.title: Patricia Routledge Remembers
programme.desc: Dame Patricia Routledge recalls `Miss Pym's Day Out', in which she portrayed legendary author Barbara Pym in an RTS Award-winning episode of Bookmark, set on the day of the 1977 Booker Prize Awards.

programme.title: Bookmark
programme.desc: After a 14 year dry spell, novelist, Barbara Pym is nominated for a Booker Prize in 1977 for her novel `Quartet in Autumn'. A look at the day of the prize presentation, as she observes people and reminisces about life and love.

programme.title: Patricia Routledge Remembers
programme.desc: `Talking Heads' was Alan Bennett's acclaimed series of one-off tele-plays, written specifically for a selection of some of his favourite actors, including the great Patricia Routledge.

programme.title: Talking Heads
programme.desc: Irene Ruddock's mother died some years ago and she lives alone. A one-woman Neighbourhood Watch scheme, her habit of writing letters to the appropriate authorities gets ridiculously out of hand.

programme.title: Wild
programme.desc: How thousands of strange nocturnal birds make their home on the tiny island of Bardsey in North Wales, and an exploration of the rich history of the island itself.

programme.title: Storyville
programme.desc: A bittersweet and surreal summer unfolds inside a crumbling Soviet-era wellness resort in Odesa, where guests seek healing, love and distraction. Once a jewel of Soviet medicine, the brutalist complex now stands as a surreal time capsule.

programme.title: Blood and Gold: The Making of Spain with Simon Sebag Montefiore
programme.desc: Simon explores Spain's golden age under Philip II through to the Spanish Civil War and dictatorship under Franco, from which Spain has emerged as a modern democratic monarchy.

programme.title: Canal Boat Diaries
programme.desc: Narrowboater Robbie Cumming begins his 170-mile journey across the north of England and soon runs into difficulty when he encounters a propeller problem in Wigan and runs aground in Blackburn. Nevertheless, he pushes on to navigate a true wonder of the waterways: the Burnley Embankment.

programme.title: Archaeology: A Secret History
programme.desc: Archaeologist Richard Miles shows how discoveries in the 18th and 19th centuries overturned ideas of when and where civilisation began, as empires competed to `own' the past.

programme.title: Thatcher: A Very British Revolution
programme.desc: As Mrs Thatcher's government transforms the British economy, tensions erupt within her inner circle and relationships in her own family are exposed. Mrs Thatcher's forthright style has led to her being viewed as domineering and unsympathetic.

programme.title: Margaret
programme.desc: On 12th November 1990, Thatcher is preparing for her speech at the Lord Mayor's banquet at the Guildhall, while Geoffrey Howe, her quietly-spoken former foreign secretary and chancellor, is penning the resignation speech that was to stun the country and seal her fate. The next day, Howe makes his lethal speech in the Houses of Parliament and the final ten days of Margaret Thatcher's reign begin.

programme.title: How to Get Ahead
programme.desc: Stephen Smith explores the flamboyant Baroque court of the Sun King, Louis XIV. Louis created the Palace of Versailles so he could surround himself with aristocrats, artists, interior designers, gardeners, wigmakers, chefs and musicians. Hordes of ambitious courtiers scrambled to get close to the king, but unseemly goings-on in the royal bedchamber reflected the quickest path to power.
